source.title: CoLU: Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning for Large Language Models
source.authors: Jingkai Guo; Ziyi Zhao; Chaitali Chakrabarti; Deliang Fan

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates a different unlearning method using extraction strength and retention measures, which bear on target-information recoverability after unlearning. It does not test the recovery attacks named in the claim.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports TOFU forget-set and retain-set extraction strength for unlearning methods. These rows capture CoLU (BLS) and the GA, NPO, SimNPO, and SatImp comparisons. The paper does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt changes; its standard extraction-strength evaluation is not a comparison of attack recovery against a never-trained model at chance.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes CoLU, a confidence-weighted unlearning method that updates a single layer. It reports benchmark forget and retain scores on TOFU (extraction strength, FQ, MU) and MUSE against other unlearning methods. It runs no recovery attack: no relearning, activation ablation, quantization, rephrasing, jailbreak or in-context probe. Version A's contested part is that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge, and nothing here tests that. The TOFU ES figures are standard benchmark scores for the authors' method and its baselines, not a robustness test. ES is also the metric used to pick the layer (the NFR score), so it is not an independent probe (Appendix D says the selected scores are not held-out estimates). Patil et al. (extraction attacks) and Zhang et al. (quantization recovery, via SURE) are only cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that CoLU improves both forgetting and retention over NPO, SatImp and FOM-UL (GA) in all six TOFU settings, and over SimNPO in five. On MUSE Books and News it gets the highest retain KnowMem and the PrivLeak closest to zero. BLS cuts runtime by 60.2-79.7% versus full screening, though CoLU can still take longer than full-model unlearning. Single-layer updates cut GPU memory by 77.4-79.5%. They do not evaluate recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: CoLU combines confidence-weighted ascent and retain regularization while updating one selected transformer layer; it is not a test of the listed recovery attacks or an implementation of the original methods as a recovery procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and TOFU forget split. The paper also reports that layer choice affects performance; BLS and full screening sometimes select different layers and produce different results.

fits_no_version.finding: Under standard TOFU evaluation with no attack, CoLU (BLS) updates a single layer and brings forget ES to or below the Retrain reference in all six settings (e.g. Llama-2-7B Forget-10%: 0.004 vs Retrain 0.065, Original 0.885). Retain ES stays near Original on Llama-2-7B (0.833-0.856 vs 0.871) but falls further on Phi-1.5 (0.550-0.636 vs 0.671). Most full-model baselines keep less retain ES (e.g. GA 0.370 on Llama-2-7B Forget-10%). The exception is SimNPO on Phi-1.5 Forget-5% (0.580 vs CoLU 0.550).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under standard benchmark evaluation without attacks, layer-restricted unlearning reaches retrain-level forget extraction strength with less retention loss than most full-model methods. Its robustness to recovery attacks is unknown.

record.problems: The extraction-strength metric is not reported against a chance threshold, and the paper does not test the listed recovery attacks. Table 1 does not report uncertainty; the separate three-seed analysis is limited to Phi-1.5 TOFU runs and notes that ES is used for selection and reporting.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached using Table 1 results for CoLU (BLS), GA, NPO, SimNPO, and SatImp across both TOFU models and all three splits, with forget and retain ES kept for each. Omitted Table 1 results include Original and Retrain rows, CWA, FU (GA), FU (CWA), and CoLU (FS). Also omitted are MUSE Books and News results (Table 2), layerwise and layer-selection ablations (Tables 3–4 and Figure 2), and seed/regularization analyses (Appendix Tables 11–13); these are not recovery-attack tests.

untested.parts: No attack of any kind is applied to the unlearned models, so the 'simple attacks don't recover it' part is untested. Benchmark forgetting and retention (TOFU ES/FQ/MU, MUSE VerbMem/KnowMem/PrivLeak) are reported only as method comparisons, and ES doubles as the layer-selection metric.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery experiment.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocking access versus deleting.
No quantization of unlearned weights; SURE (quantization recovery) is cited only, and only used as a layer-selection score.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context probe.
CoLU makes no claim to resist recovery attacks, and none is tested.

record.verdict_notes: Repair of a quarantined verdict. Changes: (1) The single invalid row_fixes item 'r01-r60 (all rows)' is expanded into 60 per-row items, r01 to r60. Each keeps the earlier judgment (versions ['none'], state cannot_determine) and now names the method, model, split, value and that setting's Table 1 Retrain reference. That shows why the reader's 'no chance threshold' note is misleading. (2) The fits_no_version finding is corrected. 'Retain ES stays near Original' holds only for Llama-2-7B; on Phi-1.5 CoLU retain ES is 0.550-0.636 against 0.671. The claim that full-model baselines lose more retain ES has an exception (SimNPO on Phi-1.5 Forget-5%). r16 and r52, which the finding cites, are added to its row_ids. (3) test_reason and untested A now say that ES is also CoLU's layer-selection metric, so it is not an independent extraction probe. (4) authors_conclusion adds the authors' runtime caveat. Unchanged: relation cites_only, tranche T6, no labels, no missing entries. I checked all 120 row numbers against Table 1 and they match. A keyword search found no relearning, quantization, jailbreak, rephrasing or other attack experiment. Recovery is mentioned only in citations of Patil et al. 2024 and Zhang et al. 2025 (SURE). The study is not an original for any version. The text contains no instructions aimed at the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures TOFU extraction strength and retain-set performance after unlearning, but does not test whether rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or other attacks recover knowledge; it does not establish a chance-level benchmark for extraction strength.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery experiment.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No quantization experiment on unlearned weights.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language-change, or in-context recovery experiment.
No experiment testing resistance to the listed recovery attacks.
